CRITICAL REFRAMING: Perfect autocorrelations (r=1.000) at lag 7 (pendulum_lab, 36 readings) and lag 14 (resonator_obs, 12 readings) with far-above-chance exact repetitions indicate cyclical or recycled measurement procedure, not independent instrumental drift. Universal weak cross-checks (all r near ±0.2, at or below chance) now suggest that 'drift' signal is an artifact of baseline vs post-baseline collection protocol difference, not environmental stressor. Shared environmental hypothesis (p=0.62) is now implausible because both obs instruments show 'parallel drift' only relative to lab instruments—but if measurement procedure differs between baseline and post-baseline phases, and if baseline and post-baseline cohorts have different N and operator workflow, apparent drift is statistical, not physical. Hypothesis 1 revised DOWN to p=0.15. Hypothesis 4 (procedural artifact) revised UP to p=0.72 because the exact repetition evidence and perfect autocorrelations directly implicate measurement protocol as the confound, not environmental stressor. Remaining hypotheses (1–3, single-instrument thermal) all revised DOWN to p=0.04 each because they assume independent samples; if samples are partially recycled or procedure-locked, thermal hypothesis is meaningless. Residual raised to p=0.05. IMMEDIATE ACTION: Do not run new trials or make predictions. Audit the trial metadata in detail: verify operator identity, time-of-day, apparatus state (e.g., warm-up time, recalibration), and equipment initialization protocol for baseline vs post-baseline phases. Check whether post-baseline readings overlap with or repeat any baseline readings. Check trial numbering for gaps or reruns. This is now a protocol audit, not a physics problem.
